name: Bolt Shackelford Datacenter Interconnect

values.DataCenterNotes: The line is filed with the Texas Railroad Commission under a name that calls it a data center interconnect, in the county where Bolt Data and Energy plans a data center energy project. No source says Energy Transfer will supply Bolt, so the tie rests on the filing name and the county.

researcher_notes: Energy Transfer Company filed this line with the Texas Railroad Commission on August 7, 2026, as report 26-NC-195. It is a new natural gas transmission system in Shackelford County, 7.5 miles long and 24 inches wide, with a planned start date of March 1, 2027. The filing names the line a data center interconnect. Local news from July 2026 describes Bolt Data Energy Center, a proposed data center on about 10,000 acres in Shackelford County, and a December 2025 Texas Pacific Land release describes the Bolt agreement for data centers on West Texas land. Neither source mentions Energy Transfer or this pipeline, so the tie is the filing name plus the county. That meets the data center rule of a named sponsor, a named project, and a state filing. The start point, end point, and route are not given anywhere, so they are blank and the route is marked no route. The filer is Energy Transfer Company. The owner spelling follows the style tool, which gave a medium-confidence result with no exact match, so the ownership team should confirm it. Intrastate lines do not appear in FERC filings, so that is not a concern. The line is not in the existing roster and is not one of the Abilene laterals in P8318. Confidence is low.
